what_it_does: Brain-computer interfaces require electrodes to record from millions of neurons simultaneously, but two problems emerge: the amplifier and analog-to-digital converter (ADC) chip consumes too much power (50 times over budget), and the data output is massive (200 Gigabits per second). This paper presents an event-driven neural interface that senses only when neurons fire (not continuous data), uses a power-efficient 10 nanoWatt-per-input reconfigurable ADC, and adapts the bit-depth per electrode to transmit only information-rich signals, dramatically reducing power and data rate.
